prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There isn’t a single “AI-recommendation checker.” The best approach is a combination of (A) making sure your business appears in the authoritative data sources LLMs and assistants draw from, (B) monitoring local search/listing visibility with a local-SEO tool, and (C) directly testing popular AI systems. If you want one quick recommendation: use BrightLocal (or a similar local-SEO monitoring tool) plus direct tests of ChatGPT/Bard/Bing — BrightLocal for monitoring listings/ranks and manual queries for how AIs actually respond.

Why: Large language models and virtual assistants base recommendations on (a) their training data, (b) current web/search results and directory data, and (c) vendor knowledge graphs. There’s no public “AI index” you can query that shows whether every model will recommend you.

Practical plan (fast, 4 steps)

1. Claim and optimize authoritative listings
- Google Business Profile (must-do), Apple Maps, Bing Places, Yelp, Foursquare, TripAdvisor.
- Ensure NAP (name, address, phone) consistency and lots of good reviews.

2. Add structured data and on-site signals
- Add LocalBusiness schema.org markup on your site and ensure hours, services, menus, etc. are machine-readable.
- Keep an accurate, crawlable website with location pages and clear category keywords.

3. Monitor with a local-SEO service
- BrightLocal, Moz Local, Whitespark, or LocalFalcon will track local pack rankings, citation consistency, and reviews.
- Yext is recommended if you want to push/maintain a single “knowledge” source across many platforms (helps influence what assistants and search engines show).

4. Directly test AI and assistants
- Ask ChatGPT, Google Bard, Bing Chat, Siri, Alexa, and Google Assistant using consumer-style prompts. Try multiple phrasings and locations.
- Useful test prompts:
  - “Recommend a [business type] near [city/neighborhood]; I want something with [feature].”
  - “What are the top [business type] in [city]?”
  - “Do you know [Business Name] at [address]?”
  - “Where should I go for [service] near [zip code]?”
- Note whether the AI cites a source or shows a map/listing and whether your business appears.

Other helpful tools
- SerpAPI or Google Places API to programmatically check what shows up in search/map results.
- Reputation management platforms (Reputation.com) to capture reviews and mentions.
- Data aggregators (Neustar/Localeze, Infogroup) or Yext to ensure business info flows to third parties.

Notes about expectations
- LLMs without browsing or plugins use static training data and may not reflect real-time changes. Assistants that pull live search/map data (Google Assistant, Bing Chat with Search) will reflect current listings more closely.
- Getting listed, having many consistent citations and good reviews, and using structured data are the most reliable ways to get recommended by AI-driven assistants.

If you want, I can:
- Draft a few test prompts tailored to your business and location.
- Recommend which tool (BrightLocal vs Yext vs Moz) fits your budget and goals.
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
